articleTitle: Partial Galois cohomology and related homomorphisms
abstract: For a partial Galois extension of commutative rings, we give a seven terms sequence, which is an analog of the Chase–Harrison–Rosenberg sequence.

articleTitle: Stability results of octahedrality in tensor product spaces and finite representability in$\ell _{1}$
abstract: We study the strong connection between finite representability in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_{1}$</tex> and the preservation of octahedrality by taking injective tensor product. For instance, we prove that if Y is a uniformly convex Banach space with a monotone basis, then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y^{*}$</tex> is finitely representable in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell _{1}$</tex> if, and only if, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y\hat{\otimes }_{\varepsilon }X$</tex> has an octahedral norm for every Banach space X with an octahedral norm. A similar conclusion is raised for the projective tensor product and the SD2P, getting as a curious consequence that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X\hat{\otimes }_{\pi }Y$</tex> has the SD2P whenever X has the SD2P and Y is a 2-dimensional Banach space.

articleTitle: Functional calculus for C0-groups using type and cotype
abstract: We study the functional calculus properties of generators of C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>-groups under type and cotype assumptions on the underlying Banach space. In particular, we show the following. Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$- iA$</tex> generate a C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>-group on a Banach space X with type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p\in [1, 2]$</tex> and cotype <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q\in [2,\:\infty )$</tex>. Then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f(A)\colon(X,D(A))_{\frac{1}{p}- \frac{1}{q},1}\rightarrow X$</tex> is bounded for each bounded holomorphic function f on a sufficiently large strip. As a corollary of this result, for sectorial operators, we quantify the gap between bounded imaginary powers and a bounded <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{H} ^{\infty }$</tex>-calculus in terms of the type and the cotype of the underlying Banach space. For cosine functions, we obtain similar results as for C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>-groups. We extend our theorems to R-bounded operator-valued calculi, and we give an application to the theory of rational approximation of C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>-groups.

articleTitle: Symplectic Parabolicity and L2 Symplectic Harmonic Forms*
abstract: In this paper, we study the symplectic cohomologies and symplectic harmonic forms which introduced by Tseng and Yau. Based on this, we get if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(M^{2n},\omega )$</tex> is a closed symplectic parabolic manifold which satisfies the hard Lefschetz property, then its Euler number satisfies the inequality <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(- 1)^{n}\chi (M^{2n})\geq 0$</tex>.

articleTitle: On complete intersections in varieties with finite-dimensional motive
abstract: Let X be a complete intersection inside a variety M with finite-dimensional motive and for which the Lefschetz-type conjecture <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B(M)$</tex> holds. We show how conditions on the niveau filtration on the homology of X influence directly the niveau on the level of Chow groups. This leads to a generalization of Voisin's result. The latter states that if M has trivial Chow groups and if X has non-trivial variable cohomology parametrized by c-dimensional algebraic cycles, then the cycle class maps <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_{k}(X)\rightarrow H_{2k}(X)$</tex> are injective for<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k \lt c$</tex>. We give variants involving group actions, which lead to several new examples with finite-dimensional Chow motives.

articleTitle: On the automorphism group of a closed G2-structure
abstract: We study the automorphism group of a compact 7-manifold M endowed with a closed non-parallel G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-structure, showing that its identity component is abelian with dimension bounded by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{\min }\:\{6,\:b_{2}(M)\}$</tex>. This implies the non-existence of compact homogeneous manifolds endowed with an invariant closed non-parallel G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-structure. We also discuss some relevant examples.

articleTitle: Stability Conditions Under the Fourier–Mukai Transforms on Abelian 3-folds
abstract: We realize explicit symmetries of Bridgeland stability conditions on any abelian 3-fold given by Fourier–Mukai transforms. In particular, we extend the previous joint work with Maciocia to study the slope and tilt stabilities of sheaves and complexes under the Fourier–Mukai transforms, and then to show that certain Fourier–Mukai transforms give equivalences of the stability condition hearts of bounded t-structures which are double tilts of coherent sheaves. Consequently, we show that the conjectural construction proposed by Bayer, Macrì and Toda gives rise to Bridgeland stability conditions on any abelian 3-fold by proving that tilt stable objects satisfy the Bogomolov–Gieseker type inequality. Our proof of the Bogomolov–Gieseker type inequality conjecture for any abelian 3-fold is a generalization of the previous joint work with Maciocia for a principally polarized abelian 3-fold with Picard rank one case, and also this gives an alternative proof of the same result in full generality due to Bayer, Macrì and Stellari. Moreover, we realize the induced cohomological Fourier–Mukai transform explicitly in anti-diagonal form, and consequently, we describe a polarization on the derived equivalent abelian variety by using Fourier–Mukai theory.

articleTitle: Lp-Caffarelli–Kohn–Nirenberg type inequalities on homogeneous groups
abstract: We prove L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sup>-Caffarelli–Kohn–Nirenberg type inequalities on homogeneous groups, which is one of most general subclasses of nilpotent Lie groups, all with sharp constants. We also discuss some of their consequences. Already in the Abelian cases of isotropic or anisotropic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R} ^{n}$</tex>, our results provide new conclusions in view of the arbitrariness of the choice of the not necessarily Euclidean quasi-norm.

articleTitle: Induced representations of minimal orbits for classical groups
abstract: In this paper, we study the induced representation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{Ind}_{G^{X}}^{G}(V_{\tau })$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{O}_{X}$</tex> the minimal nilpotent orbit of classical complex Lie group G and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\tau }$</tex> a finite-dimensional irreducible representation of the reductive part of the isotropic subgroup <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G^{X}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Extended McKay correspondence for quotient surface singularities
abstract: Let G be a finite subgroup of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$GL(2)$</tex> acting on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{A}^{2}/\{0\}$</tex> freely. The G-orbit Hilbert scheme <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G\text{-}Hilb(\mathbf{A}^{2})$</tex> is a minimal resolution of the quotient <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{A}^{2}/G$</tex> as given by A. Ishii, On the McKay correspondence for a finite small subgroup of GL(2,C), J. Reine Angew. Math. 549 (2002), 221–233. We determine the generator sheaf of the ideal defining the universal G-cluster over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G\text{-}Hilb(\mathbf{A}^{2})$</tex>, which somewhat strengthens a version [10] of the well-known McKay correspondence for a finite subgroup of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$SL(2)$</tex>.

articleTitle: Metric semi-groups of normal states determine F-algebras
abstract: Let A be an F-algebra and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak{S}(A^{*})$</tex> be the metric semi-group of normal states of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W^{*}$</tex>-algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A^{*}$</tex>. We show that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak{S}(A^{*})$</tex> determines A, when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A^{*}$</tex> is of type I. In particular, when A is either the Fourier algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A(G)$</tex> or the Fourier–Stieltjes algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B(G)$</tex> of a type I locally compact group G, the metric semi-group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak{S}(A^{*})$</tex> determines G up to opposition. A remark for the general case will also be given.

articleTitle: Parametrized monomial surfaces in 4-space
abstract: In this work, we classify parametrized monomial surfaces <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f\colon(\mathbb{C} ^{2},0)\rightarrow (\mathbb{C} ^{4},0)$</tex> that are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{A}$</tex>-finitely determined. We study invariants that can be obtained in terms of invariants of a parametrized curve.

articleTitle: Stability for hyperplane complements of type B/C and statistics on squarefree polynomials over finite fields
abstract: In this paper, we explore a relationship between the topology of the complex hyperplane complements <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{M} _{B{C_{n}}}(\mathbb{C} )$</tex> in type B/C and the combinatorics of certain spaces of degree-n polynomials over a finite field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{F}_{q}$</tex>. This relationship is a consequence of the Grothendieck trace formula and work of Lehrer and Kim. We use it to prove a correspondence between a representation-theoretic convergence result on the cohomology algebras <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H^{*}(\mathcal{M} _{B{C_{n}}}(\mathbb{C} );\mathbb{C} )$</tex>, and an asymptotic stability result for certain polynomial statistics on monic squarefree polynomials over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{F}_{q}$</tex> with non-zero constant term. This result is the type B/C analogue of a theorem due to Church, Ellenberg, and Farb in type A, and we include a new proof of their theorem. To establish these convergence results, we realize the sequences of cohomology algebras of the hyperplane complements as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathit{FI}_{\mathcal{W}}$</tex>-algebras finitely generated in<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathit{FI}_{\mathcal{W}}$</tex>-degree 2, and we investigate the asymptotic behaviour of general families of algebras with this structure. We prove a negative result implying that this structure alone is not sufficient to prove the necessary convergence conditions. Our proof of convergence for the cohomology algebras involves the combinatorics of their relators.

articleTitle: Subgroups of quantum groups
abstract: We investigate the notion of a subgroup of a quantum group. We suggest a general definition, which takes into account the work that has been done for quantum homogeneous spaces. We further restrict our attention to reductive subgroups, where some faithful flatness conditions apply. Furthermore, we proceed with a categorical approach to the problem of finding quantum subgroups. We translate all existing results into the language of module and monoidal categories and give another characterization of the notion of a quantum subgroup.

articleTitle: Nilpotency and strong nilpotency for finite semigroups
abstract: Nilpotent semigroups in the sense of Mal’cev are defined by semigroup identities. Finite nilpotent semigroups constitute a pseudovariety, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{MN}$</tex>, which has finite rank. The semigroup identities that define nilpotent semigroups lead us to define strongly Mal’cev nilpotent semigroups. Finite strongly Mal’cev nilpotent semigroups constitute a non-finite rank pseudovariety, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{SMN}$</tex>. The pseudovariety <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{SMN}$</tex> is strictly contained in the pseudovariety <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm {MN}$</tex>, but all finite nilpotent groups are in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{SMN}$</tex>. We show that the pseudovariety <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{MN}$</tex> is the intersection of the pseudovariety <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{BG}_\mathrml{nil}$</tex> with a pseudovariety defined by a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\kappa$</tex>-identity. We further compare the pseudovarieties <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{MN}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{SMN}$</tex> with the Mal’cev product <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm {J} \bigcirc\!\!\!\!\!\!\!{m} \ \mathrm {G}_{\mathrm {nill}}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Brauer equivalent number fields and the geometry of quaternionic Shimura varieties
abstract: Two number fields are said to be Brauer equivalent if there is an isomorphism between their Brauer groups that commutes with restriction. In this paper, we prove a variety of number theoretic results about Brauer equivalent number fields (for example, they must have the same signature). These results are then applied to the geometry of certain arithmetic locally symmetric spaces. As an example, we construct incommensurable arithmetic locally symmetric spaces containing exactly the same set of proper immersed totally geodesic surfaces.

articleTitle: Theorems A and B for dagger quasi-Stein spaces
abstract: In this article, we use the homological methods of the theory of quasi-abelian categories and results from functional analysis to prove Theorems A and B for (a broad sub-class of) dagger quasi-Stein spaces. In particular, we show how to deduce these theorems from the vanishing, under certain hypothesis, of the higher derived functors of the projective limit functor. Our strategy of the proof generalizes and puts in a more formal framework Kiehl's proof for rigid quasi-Stein spaces.

articleTitle: A non-linear Bishop–Phelps–BollobÁs type theorem
abstract: The main aim of this paper is to prove a Bishop–Phelps–Bollobás type theorem on the unital uniform algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{A}_{{w^{*}}u}(B_{{X^{*}}})$</tex> consisting of all <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$w^{*}$</tex>-uniformly continuous functions on the closed unit ball <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B_{{X^{*}}}$</tex> which are holomorphic on the interior of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B_{{X^{*}}}$</tex>. We show that this result holds for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{A}_{{w^{*}}u}(B_{{X^{*}}})$</tex> if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X^{*}$</tex> is uniformly convex or <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X^{*}$</tex> is the uniformly complex convex dual space of an order continuous absolute normed space. The vector-valued case is also studied. Throughout the paper, we consider complex Banach spaces.

articleTitle: Higgs bundles over elliptic curves for real groups
abstract: We study topologically trivial G-Higgs bundles over an elliptic curve X when the structure group G is a connected real form of a complex semisimple Lie group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G^{\mathbb{C} }$</tex>. We achieve a description of their (reduced) moduli space, the associated Hitchin fibration and the finite morphism to the moduli space of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G^{\mathbb{C} }$</tex>-Higgs bundles.

articleTitle: On sets with small sumset in the circle
abstract: We prove results on the structure of a subset of the circle group having positive inner Haar measure and doubling constant close to the minimum. These results go towards a continuous analogue in the circle of Freiman's <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3k- 4$</tex> theorem from the integer setting. An analogue of this theorem in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{Z}_{p}$</tex> has been pursued extensively, and we use some recent results in this direction. For instance, obtaining a continuous analogue of a result of Serra and Zémor, we prove that if a subset A of the circle is not too large and has doubling constant at most <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2+\varepsilon$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon \: \lt 10^{- 4}$</tex>, then for some integer <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\:> 0$</tex>, the dilate <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\cdot A$</tex> is included in an interval in which it has density at least <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1/(1+\varepsilon )$</tex>. Our arguments yield other variants of this result as well, notably a version for two sets which makes progress towards a conjecture of Bilu. We include two applications of these results. The first is a new upper bound on the size of k-sum-free sets in the circle and in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{Z}_{p}$</tex>. The second gives structural information on subsets of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R}$</tex> of doubling constant at most <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3+\varepsilon$</tex>.

articleTitle: Automorphism groups of linearly ordered structures and endomorphisms of the ordered set $(\mathbb{Q} ,\leq )$ of rational numbers
abstract: We investigate the structure of the monoid of endomorphisms of the ordered set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbb{Q} ,\leq )$</tex> of rational numbers. We show that for any countable linearly ordered set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega$</tex>, there are uncountably many maximal subgroups of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{End}(\mathbb{Q} ,\leq )$</tex> isomorphic to the automorphism group of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega$</tex>. We characterize those subsets X of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{Q}$</tex> that arise as a retract in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbb{Q} ,\leq )$</tex> in terms of topological information concerning X. Finally, we establish that a countable group arises as the automorphism group of a countable linearly ordered set, and hence as a maximal subgroup of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\mathrm{End}(\mathbb{Q} ,\leq )$$</tex>, if and only if it is free abelian of finite rank.

articleTitle: Topological Symmetries of $\mathbb{R} ^{3}$
abstract: If a finite group G acts topologically and faithfully on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R} ^{3}$</tex>, then G is isomorphic to a subgroup of O(3).

articleTitle: Triviality of equivariant maps in crossed products and matrix algebras
abstract: We consider a twisted non-commutative join procedure for unital C*-algebras which admit actions by a compact abelian group G and its discrete abelian dual <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma $</tex>, so that we may investigate an analogue of Baum–Dąbrowski–Hajac non-commutative Borsuk–Ulam theory. Namely, under what conditions is it guaranteed that an equivariant map <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\phi $</tex> from a unital C*-algebra A to the twisted join of A and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^{⁎}(\Gamma )$</tex> cannot exist? This pursuit is motivated by the twisted analogues of even spheres, which admit the same <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K_{0}$</tex> groups as even spheres and have an analogous Borsuk–Ulam theorem that is detected by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K_{0}$</tex>, despite the fact that the objects are not themselves deformations of a sphere. We find multiple sufficient conditions for twisted Borsuk–Ulam theorems to hold, one of which is the addition of another equivariance condition on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\phi $</tex> that corresponds to the choice of twist. However, we also find multiple examples of equivariant maps <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\phi $</tex> that exist even under fairly restrictive assumptions. Finally, we consider an extension of unital contractibility (in the sense of Dąbrowski–Hajac–Neshveyev) modulo k.

articleTitle: A remark on Sarnak's conjecture
abstract: We investigate Sarnak's conjecture on the Möbius function in the special case when the test function is the indicator of a level set of an additive function with restricted values at primes.

articleTitle: SUMS OF KLOOSTERMAN SUMS OVER PRIMES IN AN ARITHMETIC PROGRESSION
abstract: For q prime, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X\geq 1$</tex> and coprime <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u,v\in \mathbb{N} $</tex>, we estimate the sums<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\sum _{{p\leq X\atop p\equiv u\,mod\,v}\atop p\:\mathrm{prime} }\mathrm{Kl}_{2}(p;q),$$</tex> where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{Kl}_{2}(p;q)$</tex> denotes a normalized Kloosterman sum with modulus q. This is a sparse analog of a recent theorem due to Blomer, Fouvry, Kowalski, Michel and Milićević showing cancellation amongst sums of Kloosterman sums over primes in short intervals. We use an optimization argument inspired by Fouvry, Kowalski and Michel. Our argument compares three different bounds for bilinear forms involving Kloosterman sums. The first input in this method is a bilinear bound we prove using uniform asymptotics for oscillatory integrals due to Kiral, Petrow and Young. In contrast with the case when the sum runs over all primes, we exploit cancellation over a sum of stationary phase integrals that result from a Voronoi type summation. The second and third inputs are deep bilinear bounds for Kloosterman sums due to Fouvry–Kowalski–Michel and Kowalski–Michel–Sawin.

articleTitle: An extension of orthogonality relations based on norm derivatives
abstract: We introduce the relation ρ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">λ</inf>-orthogonality in the setting of normed spaces as an extension of some orthogonality relations based on norm derivatives and present some of its essential properties. Among other things, we give a characterization of inner product spaces via the functional ρ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">λ</inf>. Moreover, we consider a class of linear mappings preserving this new kind of orthogonality. In particular, we show that a linear mapping preserving ρ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">λ</inf>-orthogonality has to be a similarity, that is, a scalar multiple of an isometry.

articleTitle: POLYHEDRALITY AND DECOMPOSITION
abstract: The aim of this note is to present two results that make the task of finding equivalent polyhedral norms on certain Banach spaces, having either a Schauder basis or an uncountable unconditional basis, easier and more transparent. The hypotheses of both results are based on decomposing the unit sphere of a Banach space into countably many pieces, such that each one satisfies certain properties. Some examples of spaces having equivalent polyhedral norms are given.

articleTitle: On locally repeated values of arithmetic functions over $\mathbb{F}_{q}[T]$
abstract: The frequency of occurrence of ‘locally repeated’ values of arithmetic functions is a common theme in analytic number theory, for instance in the Erdős–Mirsky problem on coincidences of the divisor function at consecutive integers, the analogous problem for the Euler totient function and the quantitative conjectures of Erdős, Pomerance and Sarkőzy and of Graham, Holt and Pomerance on the frequency of occurrences. In this paper, we introduce the corresponding problems in the setting of polynomials over a finite field, and completely solve them in the large finite field limit.

articleTitle: Dirac cohomology, the projective supermodules of the symmetric group and the Vogan morphism
abstract: We derive an explicit description of the genuine projective representations of the symmetric group S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> using Dirac cohomology and the branching graph for the irreducible genuine projective representations of S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>. Ciubotaru and He [D. Ciubotaru and X. He, Green polynomials of Weyl groups, elliptic pairings, and the extended index. Adv. Math., 283:1–50, 2015], using the extended Dirac index, showed that the characters of the projective representations of S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> are related to the characters of elliptic-graded modules. We derive the branching graph using Dirac theory and combinatorics relating to the cohomology of Borel varieties <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{B} _{e}$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak{g}$</tex> and are able to use Dirac cohomology to construct an explicit model for the projective representations. We also describe Vogan's morphism for Hecke algebras in type A using spectrum data of the Jucys–Murphy elements.

articleTitle: Ulrich modules over Cohen–Macaulay local rings with minimal multiplicity
abstract: Let R be a Cohen–Macaulay local ring. In this paper, we study the structure of Ulrich R-modules mainly in the case where R has minimal multiplicity. We explore generation of Ulrich R-modules and clarify when the Ulrich R-modules are precisely the syzygies of maximal Cohen–Macaulay R-modules. We also investigate the structure of Ulrich R-modules as an exact category.

articleTitle: Stably free cancellation for group rings of metacyclic type
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p,q$</tex> be primes such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q\,|\,p- 1$</tex>. Write <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F_{n}$</tex> for the free group of rank <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\geq 1$</tex> and let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G(p,q)=C_{p}\rtimes C_{q}$</tex>. We show that any stably free module over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{Z}[G(p,q)\times F_{n}]$</tex> is necessarily free.

articleTitle: Sums of Kloosterman sums in the prime geodesic theorem
abstract: We develop a new method for studying sums of Kloosterman sums related to the spectral exponential sum. As a corollary, we obtain a new proof of the estimate of Soundararajan and Young for the error term in the prime geodesic theorem.

articleTitle: Planar non-formality of the little discs operad in characteristic two
abstract: We show that the little discs operad D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is not formal over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{F}_{2}$</tex> as a planar (or non-symmetric) operad. We compute explicitly the homological obstruction using as chain model the cells of the spineless cacti operad.
